# kimage

> kimage declares immutable, versioned container images as Kubernetes resources,
> manages their production and verified publication to a retained cluster-local
> registry, and resolves workload image selectors to digest-pinned pulls. Apache
> 2.0. Alpha. Public Cargo packages: kimage-core and kimage-control, version 0.2.0.

**When to use it.** Use kimage when inputs are already provisioned in Kubernetes,
when images should remain available independently of source/build cache, or when
a cluster needs local build and pull workflows without an external registry.
Application authors declare an Image, exact version, and source; the controller
handles attempts and publication. There is no per-image BuildRun or output
registry configuration. kpack also declares images; kimage specifically combines
immutable versions, retained local storage, and integrated workload resolution.
Shipwright provides configurable build strategies; Tekton handles general task
pipelines. The current kimage builder is narrower than those general workflows.

**Current boundaries.** Builds support Containerfile, strategy Direct,
builderRef default, FROM scratch, provisioned local files, and network-none RUN.
No remote base images, remote ADD/context URLs, external syntax frontends, remote
cache, general base provisioning, multi-platform images, signing/attestations,
HA, arbitrary storage/schema migration, or automatic retained-artifact GC.
Administrator-managed builder isolation is not a hostile tenant security claim.

**Install native commands without cloning the repository.** Requires Rust
1.99.0 or newer; ensure Cargo's bin directory is on PATH:

```sh
cargo install kimage-control --version 0.2.0 --locked
kimage-install --version
kimage-install --help
```

This installs kimage-install, kimage-operator, kimage-admission, kimage-gateway,
kimage-proxy, kimage-input, and kimage-exporter. Add --bin kimage-install for only
the installer. The unrelated crate named `kimage` belongs to another project.
Gateway/proxy report serving compatibility version 0.2.0, separately from Cargo
package version 0.2.0. kimage-bootstrap is an unpublished internal bundle helper.

**Official bundles and offline use.** No source checkout or packaging script is
needed. `kimage-install bundle-fetch` downloads and verifies the exact official
GitHub release matching this CLI package version (0.2.0), never latest, without
kubeconfig or cluster writes. It prints JSON {bundle: <verified-directory>,
trustedInventory: <sha256-digest>}. All bundle-using phases use the same automatic
selection and reverify cached files before reuse. `--release 0.2.0` pins an exact
release; `--bundle-cache <directory>` overrides the private cache. Default cache:
XDG_CACHE_HOME/kimage/bundles if set, otherwise ~/Library/Caches/kimage/bundles on
macOS or ~/.cache/kimage/bundles on Linux. `--offline` refuses network access and
fails clearly on a cache miss. Keep an independent bundle copy for recovery.

The fixed official inferal-oss/kimage GitHub repository over verified HTTPS is
the online trust origin. GitHub's API provides asset size/SHA-256; the client
restricts HTTPS download origins, verifies archive/inventory/static executables
and complete OCI graphs, rejects unsafe/oversized tar entries, and atomically
caches only complete verified content. Public downloads need no token. Optional
KIMAGE_GITHUB_TOKEN authenticates only the fixed metadata endpoint for API rate
limits; it is never sent to asset downloads or redirects.
For air gaps, transfer the fetched bundle directory and inventory digest through
your approved channel. Supply `--bundle <directory> --trusted-inventory
sha256:<64-lowercase-hex-digits>` instead of --release. Local bundles always need
that independent pin. The pin is also optional for official downloads. Cache
corruption fails closed and requires explicit removal/refetch. GitHub Actions
builds complete Linux/amd64 bundles and native Linux/amd64 and macOS/arm64
installers, inventories, checksums, and license notices as release assets.
Official bundles start at 0.2.0; 0.1.0 has no downloadable bundle assets.

```sh
kimage-install bundle-fetch
kimage-install bundle-check --offline
```

**Cluster setup is a separate administrator prerequisite.** Automatic bundle
delivery does not provision Kubernetes. Supply administrator kubeconfig, issuer
credentials, persistent storage, cached carrier, and the supported runtime.
The full acceptance fixture uses Kubernetes v1.36.5+k3s1, containerd
2.3.4-k3s1.36, Linux/amd64, Ubuntu 24.04.5, kernel 6.8.0-142. Choose
--runtime-profile k3s explicitly. The CLI default inferal profile checks the
earlier RKE2 v1.36.5+rke2r1 / containerd 2.3.4-k3s1 foundation profile.
Untested exact runtime versions are refused. A generic kind/k3d/container cluster
is not automatically supported: user namespaces, idmapped volumes, kernel and
filesystem support, CNI policy enforcement, and persistent storage all matter.

Required installation arguments are --runtime-profile, --namespace (system),
--application-namespace (distinct), --installation, --node, --carrier (approved
digest already cached on that node), --storage-class, --port (at least 1024),
--credentials (registry directory). Bundle selection is automatic; optionally add
--release 0.2.0, or the local bundle/pin pair described above. Use an
administrator kubeconfig. Preserve identical arguments across resumable phases:
bootstrap, seed, handover, control-plane with --admission-credentials, then builder
with --builder-credentials. Run `kimage-install <phase> --help` for exact flags.
No SSH, runtime socket, host filesystem mount, or node trust-store edit is used.
Missing carrier or incompatible namespace policy fails rather than falling back.

Registry credentials: ca.crt, tls.crt, tls.key, distinct reader-password and
publisher-password; leaf SAN <installation>-registry.<system-namespace>.svc.
Admission: ca.crt, tls.crt, tls.key, resolution-key (at least 32 bytes); leaf SAN
<installation>-admission.<system-namespace>.svc. Builder: ca.crt, server.crt,
server.key, client.crt, client.key; server SAN
<installation>-builder.<system-namespace>.svc, separate server/client EKUs.
CA private keys stay outside Kubernetes. The seven-day test issuer is only a
development fixture. Builder uses BuildKit 0.33.0 / builtin frontend 1.27.0,
hostUsers:false, native snapshotter, no host/runtime mounts or service account
token, and nested namespace capabilities with unconfined seccomp/AppArmor inside
its Pod. It needs administrator-approved policy and denies worker egress.

**Minimal complete build example.** Assumes namespace apps and default builder
are already configured. On Linux/amd64 with Rust and a musl linker, create a small
program in hello.rs: `fn main() { println!("Hello from kimage!"); loop {
std::thread::park_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(3600)); } }`.

```sh
rustup target add x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
rustc --edition=2024 --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl \
  -C opt-level=z -C strip=symbols -C panic=abort hello.rs -o hello
kubectl -n apps create configmap hello-context --from-file=hello=./hello \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```

On macOS use a Linux/amd64 machine or build container for that executable; a
native macOS binary cannot run inside the scratch image. Save as image.yaml:

```yaml
apiVersion: kimage.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Image
metadata:
  name: hello
  namespace: apps
spec:
  version: "1.0.0"
  platform: {os: linux, architecture: amd64}
  source:
    build:
      format: Containerfile
      execution: {strategy: Direct, builderRef: default}
      cache: {mode: Local}
      definition:
        inline: |
          FROM scratch
          COPY hello /hello
          ENTRYPOINT ["/hello"]
      inputs:
        contextPath: /workspace/context
        volumes:
          - name: context
            configMap:
              name: hello-context
              items: [{key: hello, path: hello, mode: 365}]
        volumeMounts:
          - {name: context, mountPath: /workspace/context, readOnly: true}
```

Mode 365 is decimal for octal 0555. Apply, wait for verified publication, and run
the downloadable Deployment (or use the selector in your own Pod template):

```sh
kubectl apply -f image.yaml
kubectl -n apps wait --for=condition=Ready image/hello --timeout=10m
kubectl -n apps get imagereleases
kubectl apply -f https://kimage.dev/examples/hello/deployment.yaml
kubectl -n apps rollout status deployment/hello --timeout=5m
kubectl -n apps logs deployment/hello
```

The workload's image field is quoted YAML:

```yaml
containers:
  - name: hello
    image: "platform://apps/hello:^1.0.0"
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

Admission leaves workload templates symbolic and pins actual CREATE Pods,
including init containers, to
127.0.0.1:<port>/<namespace>/<image-uid>@sha256:<digest>, with IfNotPresent and
eligible-node constraints. Kubelet uses its normal runtime and node-local proxy.
Changing a range/channel affects newly created Pods, not existing Pods; use exact
versions for a uniform rollout. Unsupported image-update/ephemeral-container
paths are rejected. Create replacements through the workload controller.

**Selector rules.** `platform://apps/hello:1.2.4` selects that exact release;
`:^1.2.0` selects the highest compatible published release below 2.0.0;
`:~1.2.0` stays in the 1.2 patch series; `:stable` reads the explicit mapping
`spec.channels: {stable: "1.2.4"}`. A channel does not produce that version.
Colon ranges start with ^, ~, >, <, =, or *. Compound ranges such as
`platform://apps/hello:>=1.2.0, <2.0.0` work in quoted YAML. Numeric-leading
colon selectors must be complete exact versions: :1.2 and :1.2.* are rejected.
The readable query `platform://apps/hello?version=^1.2.0` and the older encoded
query `?version=%5E1.2.0` both work, decoded once. Colon selectors use literal
characters. Do not combine a colon selector with a query. Prereleases need an
explicitly matching prerelease requirement. No implicit latest, version build
metadata, or cross-namespace consumption. The application webhook is fail-closed;
its outage can block other Pod creation in scope too. Direct internal registry
references and opt-in label bypasses are not supported consumption paths.

**Image and input contracts.** Image/ImageRelease use kimage.dev/v1alpha1.
Choose exactly one source.build or source.ociArchive. An Image UID/version is
immutable after publication; differing output is VersionConflict, so request a
new exact version. Image recreation gets a new UID/repository. Published releases
survive source/Image/cache removal. ConfigMap/Secret inputs freeze UID and
resourceVersion per attempt. Mounted definitions use definition.fromFile.path;
ordinary definitions live under /workspace/inputs, secret definitions under
/run/kimage-build-secrets, independently of COPY contextPath. Mounts must be
read-only and non-overlapping. Traversal and symlink escapes are rejected.
PVC inputs need inputs.producerHandoff:true and stopped producers; this is not
an atomic filesystem snapshot. Use buildSecrets to bind declared Secret files
to RUN --mount=type=secret; keep them outside ordinary context. Secret values do
not automatically invalidate cache: use a non-sensitive cache.invalidationToken
when needed. Local cache is disposable; Disabled requests a no-cache solve.
Cancellation fences the dedicated worker and clears its cache.

OCI archive sources require a same-namespace claimName, relative path,
producerHandoff:true, and expected root {mediaType,digest,size}. Root digest is
not the archive-file checksum. Files must be readable by UID 65532. Complete
original OCI bytes, platform, compressed layer digests, and DiffIDs are verified.
Single-platform manifests/nested indexes are supported; zstd, multi-platform,
descriptor URLs/embedded data, and subject/referrer graphs are unsupported.
`kimage-install schemas` prints full CRD JSON without changing the cluster.

**Operations.** join-node uses the original installation arguments plus
--target-node and the same prerequisites. upgrade-serving takes target
--bundle/--trusted-inventory and source --previous-bundle/--previous-trusted-inventory.
Rollback reverses those independently trusted pairs. The tested actual binary
window is Distribution 3.1.1 ↔ 3.1.2 and gateway/proxy 0.1.0 ↔ 0.2.0, with the
shipped filesystem configuration on the same PVC. Prefer Distribution 3.1.2.
All non-serving component versions/roots and bundle API revision must match.
The updater uses a Lease, warmup pulls, immutable checkpoints, read-only retained
serving, and single-writer replacement. Publication pauses; interrupted streams
use runtime retry/digest checks. Repeat the same pair after interruption. It
never changes CRDs or migrates data. Whole 0.1.0/0.2.0 release bundles differ in
non-serving component roots, so this is not a general whole-release downgrade. Schema revision 4 accepts only the exact
shipped additive revision 2/3 transitions; no schema downgrade/storage migration.

recover reuses original bootstrap arguments and PVC to recreate carrier serving,
then normal phases restore components. It requires a usable control plane/node,
cached carrier, retained bundle/credentials, and original PVC. It cannot recover
lost storage. Back up the whole Distribution backend together with release
metadata, UIDs/root descriptors, and schema coordination state. Published alpha
releases are permanently pinned; deletion/unpinning is denied. No automatic GC
or explicit artifact purge. uninstall removes owned disposable components but
retains PVCs, CRDs, Images, and ImageReleases. Do not force finalizers or delete
namespaces/backends as normal cleanup. Running containers survive registry
downtime; new uncached starts can wait/fail until serving returns.

renew-tls uses cluster arguments plus --admission-credentials without bundle
arguments. It replaces validated leaves while preserving CA/password/resolution
key, then checks served fingerprints. CA/password/key rotation uses an explicit
maintenance window and retained-PVC recovery; builder mTLS uses reprovisioning.

**Optional export.** A separate administrator-enabled exporter needs approved
HTTPS origins. Image spec.exports contains named registry destinations with
repository (authority/path), explicit tags, credentialsSecretRef or explicit
unauthenticated:true, optional caSecretRef with ca.crt, and overwritePolicy:Never.
Credential Secret type is kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson, with auths matching the
exact authority/port. Basic auth or anonymous only; no Bearer exchange/helpers.
Original retained graph bytes are copied and remotely verified without a rebuild.
Existing same-digest tags are idempotent; differing tags are TagConflict. Other
writers require registry-side immutability. Export status/retries are separate
from internal Ready. Target removal/Image deletion never deletes remote content.

**Diagnostics and trust.** Read Image status.conditions/observedGeneration,
operation/releaseRef/build, separate status.exports, and normal Pod events.
Operator/admission expose /metrics on health listeners; proxy 0.2.0 exposes it
on its canonical-authority loopback listener, inspectable by API forwarding.
Stage counters/durations cover build/publication/pull without identity labels.
Check catalog/node sample completeness and timestamps before using gauges.
Admission is read-only; publishers and readers have distinct credentials.
Eligible node administrators are trusted readers; namespace routing is not
hostile-tenant image confidentiality. Native clients keep TLS verification on.
57 Rust tests run on macOS/arm64 and Linux/amd64 musl. Separate two-node
acceptance harnesses cover lifecycle/recovery/binary rollback/export and are not
ordinary CI; historical live bundles predate the latest selector/CLI metadata.

## Reference

- [Handbook, Markdown](https://kimage.dev/docs/index.md): Full tutorial, installation commands, field reference, operations, troubleshooting, and trust model.
- [Hello Image](https://kimage.dev/examples/hello/image.yaml): Complete build declaration used above.
- [Hello Deployment](https://kimage.dev/examples/hello/deployment.yaml): Complete restricted workload using a readable range.
- [Hello program](https://kimage.dev/examples/hello/main.rs): Static Linux tutorial executable source.

- [Source and issues](https://github.com/inferal-oss/kimage): Apache 2.0 repository, engineering contracts, release procedure, acceptance receipts, and contribution workflow.
